- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline after peak), model overestimates continuation; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase downward forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment-driven volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–3% in early cycles; apply +1.5% bias to first 7–10 days of forecast to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model fails to capture sentiment shifts; adjust forecast mid-horizon to reflect sentiment swing direction.
